systemSummary: The audit feature builds on the modernized .NET 8 reconciliation service (see the approved 'modernization' spec bundle). That service already produces exceptions.csv each run, classified by reason (UNSETTLED, ORPHAN_SETTLEMENT, AMOUNT_MISMATCH, DUPLICATE_TRADE_KEY). Today, analysts resolve exceptions by manually editing that CSV in place; there is no resolution API, no persistence of resolution history, and no separation between the person who proposes a resolution and the person who approves it.
components: ReconciliationService (modernized) — produces exceptions.csv per run; this feature adds a resolution workflow layered on top, keyed by exception identity (run id + trade/settlement key).
New: ExceptionResolutionApi — accepts a maker's proposed resolution (reason code + evidence) and a checker's approve/reject decision.
New: AuditEventStore — append-only persistence for every resolution lifecycle event (proposed, approved, rejected).
New: AuditExportService — reads the AuditEventStore for a date range and produces a durable export file.
Existing telemetry pipeline — structured logging/metrics infrastructure already used by the modernized reconciliation service; this feature must emit events into it without adding sensitive fields.
dataFlows: Analyst (maker) reviews an exception from exceptions.csv → submits a proposed resolution (reason code, evidence, exception identity) → ExceptionResolutionApi → AuditEventStore (event type PROPOSED).
A different analyst (checker) reviews the proposed resolution → submits approve or reject → ExceptionResolutionApi → AuditEventStore (event type APPROVED or REJECTED).
Compliance requests an export for a date range → AuditExportService reads AuditEventStore → durable export file (see REQ-8).
Every lifecycle transition also emits a telemetry event (counts and identifiers only, no trade/settlement content) to the existing telemetry pipeline.
constraints: Must build on top of the modernized .NET 8 reconciliation service; it must not require changes to the reconciliation engine's matching/classification logic.
Exception identity must be derived from data already produced by the reconciliation run (run id + TradeId + SettlementDate) since no new identifier scheme exists upstream.
The audit trail must be append-only: the data store chosen must not allow UPDATE or DELETE against existing resolution events at the application layer.

Concurrent resolution attempts (e.g. two makers proposing for the same exception, or a retried submission from a flaky client) must be handled safely without creating duplicate or conflicting final states.

No sensitive trade or settlement data (amounts, counterparty identifiers, account numbers) may appear in logs or telemetry, per existing Security policy carried over from the modernization effort's NFR-5 observability baseline.
knownBehaviors: exceptions.csv rows are uniquely identified today only by their (TradeId, SettlementDate, reason) tuple within a given run id; there is no persistent exception identifier across runs.

The modernized reconciliation service's structured run-summary log (NFR-5 in the modernization spec) contains only counts, never per-record content — this feature must preserve that same discipline for its own telemetry.
